title: A broadcast run performs ZERO on-chain verification of its own outcome: Phase 7 executes in forge's local pass, and the compensating human check is unticked

description:
A broadcast run performs ZERO on-chain verification of its own outcome: Phase 7 executes in forge's local pass, and the compensating human check is unticked

Classification basis (verbatim from the severity-classifier): Medium under C4: assets are not at direct risk, but protocol function and availability can be impacted - a half-applied one-shot cutover leaves mint paths reverting with no automated or procedural detection, because every assertion in the script evaluates before dispatch and the story's designated post-broadcast human confirmation (line 1195) is unticked. The assumptions (broadcast-time divergence) and external requirements (mainnet drift or a failed tx during the session; an operator who does not self-verify) are stated. Not High: no attacker, no theft, no unrecoverable loss, and the fork run evidences a sound happy path with zero unintended state writes.
impact: No assets are stolen, lost or made unrecoverable. The impact is on PROTOCOL FUNCTION AND AVAILABILITY: a half-applied cutover leaves one or more of the five dispatcher indices in the fail-closed intermediate state the story itself documents (`hook.setDispatcher(new)` landed, `replaceDispatcher(idx, new)` not), so mints on that index revert `OnlyDispatcher` indefinitely rather than intermittently, and nothing in the tooling raises a signal. Secondary: donor->streamer routing, batch-minter whitelist/stream registration and staker migration can each be left one-sided.
attackPath: 1. No attacker is required. The precondition is ordinary broadcast-time divergence: an on-chain revert, a state drift between the local pass and dispatch, or an operator abort mid-session.
2. `run()` executes the entire Solidity body ONCE in forge's local pass, collecting calldata; ~60 transactions are then signed on the Ledger and dispatched afterwards.

3. Every safety assertion in the script - Phase 0 preconditions, in-phase post-conditions (BPT conservation :892-895, newBM balance unchanged :728-731, `old.paused()` :1134, `V1 totalStaked == 0` :1394) and the whole of Phase 7 - has therefore ALREADY evaluated, against local pre-broadcast state, before transaction #1 leaves the machine. They assert that the PLAN is internally consistent, never that the CHAIN matches it.
4. Phase 8 (which contains the BLOCKING probes) does not execute under `--broadcast` at all.
5. The story's designated compensating control is checklist line 1195, a '(Post-broadcast, HUMAN step)' item. It is UNTICKED.
6. Net: on the broadcast path there is no outcome verification of any kind. The system can be left half-configured over live funds with no automated and no procedural detection.
recommendation:
PRIMARY (from the auditor, endorsed): Add a read-only verification entry point (e.g. `promotion-ready:verify`) that re-runs `_phase7_wiringAssertions()` as a standalone `forge script --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET` invocation against live post-broadcast state, and append it to the `:broadcast` and `:resume` npm chains after the patch script (`&& forge script ...:VerifyPromotionReady`). Phase 7 is already `internal view` and self-contained apart from the deployment addresses, which the progress file supplies - the refactor is mechanical. Until then, tick checklist line 1195 as a hard gate, not an optional sweep.

CLASSIFIER ADDENDA (both are conditions on the fix, not alternatives to it):
(1) BLOCKING FIX-ORDER DEPENDENCY - implement L-02 (PR-06) FIRST. Relocating Phase 7 to a standalone post-broadcast run re-reads `bptAtPhase0` from an already-emptied `OLD_POOLER`, which makes the 16,338.8190 BPT conservation assertion vacuous on the FRESH path too, not just on resume. Shipping M-01's fix without L-02's persisted-baseline fix would widen a sibling bug while appearing to close this one. The verification entry point must consume a PERSISTED `bptAtCutover` from the progress file, never a freshly-read Phase 0 value.
(2) ZERO-CODE INTERIM CONTROL, available for this session - tick line 1195 and line 1197 as mandatory, blocking, signed-off steps in the runbook before the Ledger key is disconnected. This does not require touching the script and discharges most of the impact on its own.
(3) Confirm, before the session, forge's actual behaviour under `--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow` when a dispatched transaction reverts on-chain (does it halt the sequence, and what exit code does it return?). This audit did NOT verify it and the finding does not depend on it - but the answer determines how much of the gap the interim control must cover.
recommendationQuality: strong - concrete, mechanical, with a named entry point and a stated ordering constraint

classification.likelihood: medium - no adversary and no special conditions; requires only that something diverges during a multi-hour, 60+-transaction Ledger session over live mainnet state. The fork dry run is evidence the HAPPY path is sound; it is not evidence about the divergent path, because the fork run was PREVIEW and Phase 7 there ran against a state the same process had just produced locally.
classification.assumptions: That at least one transaction in the broadcast sequence lands differently from, or fails relative to, the locally-simulated plan. Stated, not hidden.
classification.externalRequirements: Mainnet state drift or a transaction failure during the session; an operator who does not independently perform the unticked line-1195 on-chain confirmation.
classification.recoverability: Recoverable by owner action (all mutation targets remain owner-controlled and `migrate` / `:resume` are re-runnable) - but recovery is gated on someone NOTICING, which is precisely what this finding says is absent.

pocNote: No standalone PoC. Evidence is the run-22 mainnet-fork PREVIEW execution of `promotion-ready:dry` at block 25659373 (see the script-audit review artifacts).

storyAcceptanceTextVerbatim.text: - [x] **Hooks are REPOINTED, not redeployed** — for all five: `pull()` → `hook.setDispatcher(new)` → `newDispatcher.setHook(hook)`, in that order (fail-closed). **Zero `phUSD.setMinter` calls in the whole script**, so mint authority is byte-identical before and after **by construction**. [CORRECTED 2026-08-01 post-review — no on-chain assertion is written; the check is the post-broadcast HUMAN item at the end of this checklist. The script comment claiming Phase 7 asserts it has been fixed.]
storyAcceptanceTextVerbatim.deviation: The item is ticked and its post-review correction explicitly REASSIGNS the mint-authority check to 'the post-broadcast HUMAN item at the end of this checklist' - i.e. to line 1195. Line 1195 is UNTICKED. The correction therefore transferred the obligation to a control that has not been discharged, so no verification of mint-authority invariance exists on any path. The story's own remedy for the first drift created the second.

storyAcceptanceTextVerbatim.text: - [x] `npm run promotion-ready:dry` against live mainnet: no revert, all phase-0 and phase-7 assertions pass, no progress file written in preview.
storyAcceptanceTextVerbatim.deviation: Accurate as written FOR THE DRY RUN, and the tick is earned. The deviation is that this item is the only verification evidence the story records, while the `//promotion-ready:dry` package.json annotation presents 'Phase 7's full bidirectional wiring read-back' as the verification gate for the cutover generally. A reader of the ticked checklist is entitled to conclude the broadcast is verified; it is not. This is a scope-of-claim deviation, not a false tick.

compensatingControlStatus.text: - [ ] (Post-broadcast, HUMAN step) confirm on-chain: `configs(1..4,7)` resolve to the new dispatchers with price/growth preserved; the old DelayRelease holds 0 USDC and the old batch-minter holds 0 USDC **and is `paused()`**; **the rescued ~349 USDC (98.04 + 250.77) sits in the streamer's buffer, not on `newBM`**; the ratchet hook's 70 phUSD `mintDebt` was pulled and all five hooks now read `dispatcher == ` their new dispatcher with `ratio`/`recipient` intact; **phUSD's minter set is byte-identical to its pre-cutover state**; the new pooler holds the full 16,338.8190 BPT, is owned by the Ledger, and the old pooler holds 0; each V1 staker has `totalStaked == 0`, is unregistered from the Pauser, and its V2 counterpart holds the migrated total plus a non-zero phUSD budget; every donor's `nudgeStreamer()` returns the new streamer; `streams(newBM, USDC/phUSD/KENDU).duration` read 10/30/30 days.
compensatingControlStatus.note: This unticked item is the single most load-bearing fact in the whole classification. It is a well-specified, sufficient control; ticking it before/at the session would substantially reduce M-01's impact even with no code change. Its sibling at line 1197 ('(Post-broadcast, HUMAN step) trigger one index-4 mint and assert `BatchDonatedViaPSM` fired — a green transaction is **not** evidence for the pooler.') is also unticked.

severityDebate.whyNotHigh: C4 High requires assets stolen/lost/compromised directly or via a valid attack path with no hand-wavy hypotheticals. There is no attacker, no theft path, and no demonstrated route to unrecoverable loss - every affected contract stays owner-controlled and the fork run showed zero unintended state writes. Escalating an assurance-and-availability defect to High would be exactly the overstatement that dilutes a report.
severityDebate.whyMediumAndNotLow: Three facts jointly clear the Medium bar and none of them is hypothetical: (a) the undetected end state is a real availability impact - mint indices reverting `OnlyDispatcher` past the intended fail-closed window - not merely 'we would not have a report'; (b) the compensating control is not merely weak, it is ABSENT on the broadcast path, because the only outcome check the design defines (line 1195) is unticked at the time of this audit; (c) this defect is the ENABLING condition that converts three other Lows in this set from theoretical to undetectable - PR-11's stated backstop `require(old.totalStaked() == 0)` at :1394, PR-02's trailing `require(balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` at :1148, and PR-06's BPT conservation all evaluate in the same local pass. That is 'protocol function or availability could be impacted, with stated assumptions and external requirements' - the C4 Medium shape.

limbRejected.limb: 'a 60+-tx one-shot cutover can exit 0 while half-applied' / 'forge exiting 0 while a tx reverted on-chain'
limbRejected.ruling: EXCLUDED FROM THE SEVERITY BASIS. The fork run was PREVIEW, so forge's `--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow` receipt-handling and exit-code behaviour on a reverted on-chain transaction was NOT observed in this audit; it is reasoned, not evidenced. Under Law 1 the finding is not dropped, but an unverified limb must not carry a severity. The Medium therefore rests ONLY on the verified structural facts: Phase 7 and every in-phase assertion evaluate before dispatch (read directly from run():400-411 and the local-pass execution model), Phase 8 is gated off under broadcast (run():402-408), and line 1195 is unticked (read verbatim from the story). Those three hold regardless of what forge's exit code does.
limbRejected.actionForReport: State the exit-code question as an OPEN OPERATIONAL QUESTION for the operator to confirm before the session, not as a finding claim.

severityDebate.oneShotWeight: Applied. On a redeployable contract, 'no post-deployment verification entry point' would be routine hardening. Here the operation cannot be re-run cleanly, the operator gets one Ledger session, and the designated human backstop is unticked - which is what moves it over the line rather than merely up the Low ordering.

ledgerRelationships.relation: ADJACENT, NOT DUPLICATE. UBC-03 is a BREADTH gap (_verifyFinalState covers ~5 of ~25 mutations); PR-09 is a TIMING gap (100% of the assertions, 0% of them post-broadcast). A UBC-03-style fix - adding twenty more assertions - would not move PR-09 at all on this script, because all twenty would still evaluate in the local pass. Different fingerprint on contract, function, rootCauseClass AND entryPoint. Linked so a triager sees the family; explicitly NOT collapsed.
